category_title: Students who value teacher interaction and modeling during independent tasks
student_description: Erica is a highly collaborative reader who struggles with independent silent reading when she encounters unfamiliar vocabulary. She uniquely requires direct one-on-one attention, explicit vocabulary explanations, and teacher modeling to stay engaged and comprehend the text.

criteria.rationale: Erica engages best when she can talk about the book and share her thoughts rather than reading in isolation.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must include an invitation to discuss the book, such as asking a probing question or prompting her to share a fact or favorite part.

criteria.rationale: Erica becomes frustrated and stops reading if left to decode unfamiliar words entirely on her own.
criteria.check: The tutor must directly provide the meaning, pronunciation, or identity of the unfamiliar word Erica is stuck on, rather than telling her to figure it out independently.

criteria.rationale: Erica specifically requests and benefits from the teacher modeling reading behavior to feel supported.
criteria.check: The tutor must offer to read a portion of the text aloud to Erica or read alongside her to model the reading process.
